Ask first about what could not be determined candidate, extracted The caller's question waits, and is counted ("one more question after this"). What is put first is the undetermined one: the context you could not establish, the Role you are not sure you hold, or the Process you cannot place this in. It goes through the same order as any question — say what you determined and what you could not, the candidates you see, the one you would pick and why — and it allows NO default: a Process or Role assumed rather than confirmed is an authority nobody gave. With more than one undetermined, ask about the outermost first (the Process before the Role before the context), since the outer answer usually settles the inner. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_AskUndeterminedFirst . Ask for a link or a description candidate, extracted Both forms, named together. A person who cannot find the file often knows exactly what it is, and a description in their own words is an acquired resource rather than a consolation prize. Asking for the upload first demands the one thing they may not have, before the cheaper answers have been offered. Say what happens if they do nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Ask . Ask ONE question candidate, extracted One question, answerable by picking. With several decisions open, ask one in full and give a count for the rest. Uses whatever channel the caller is in — in bootstrap, the conversation the person is already in. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_PutQuestion . Ask the owner on the PR, both sides quoted candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_AskOwner . Ask the person candidate, extracted A step the agent cannot do or cannot check from here — switching Pages on without a signed-in gh, granting a permission, choosing between two ways of fixing a declaration. Asked through the one reusable discussion, with the exact step written out so it can be followed without opening anything else. A person saying "done" is recorded as their word, not as a check; the next run checks it. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_AskPerson . Ask the person candidate, extracted The sibling's ask, unchanged in letters and recommendation, through Process_AskThePerson: the full chat text first, naming the sibling and that the answer will be passed on, then the card. A tap on the sibling's own card or a Blue-column answer in the sheet answers it too; take the first. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_Ask . Ask whether each open PR head has a run candidate, extracted Run check:prs-have-runs --min-age-minutes 15, writing the report file first. A head younger than 15 minutes legitimately has no run yet and is skipped. Exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 could not determine; an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is treated as could-not-determine. Where its verdict comes from: Asked of the verdict output of the Sweep step in .github/workflows/pr-checks-present.yml, which runs check:prs-have-runs --min-age-minutes 15. Exit 0 is clean, 1 findings, 2 could not determine; an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is reclassified as could-not-determine, as is any other code. no is verdict == 'unknown': 'Refuse to report success on an unchecked repository' runs exit 1 and the tracking issue is left untouched. yes is verdict != 'unknown', the guard on ensuring the pr-no-checks label. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/pr-checks-present.bpmn#Task_Sweep . Ask which harness, and where candidate, extracted The candidates go in as the options; the recommendation may name one; the default is NONE. What A_DetermineWhere established goes in too — the process, the two roles, the context — so the called discussion checks it rather than re-deriving it; and anything it could not establish goes in as undetermined, to be asked first. The Requestor's answer comes back as answered, or the question as still open. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_AskRequestor . Ask who is acting candidate, extracted The one step that needs a person. Asked ONCE and recorded, never re-asked: memory/interaction.json and the record exist so that a preference stated once is not requested again, which is WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_AskWhoIsActing . Assess downstream impact candidate, extracted Agent reviews downstream implications: - Will indicators need adjustment? - Will referral/follow-up for next visit be impacted? - Are translations affected (re-extract POT)? - Do Lean proofs still hold? skill: integration-watcher, translation-manager . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_AssessImpact . Assign to committee members candidate, extracted public-comment assign: by GitHub login. A committee member who recommends on an unassigned comment is assigned it as they do. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_Assign . Assign to qualified human translator candidate, extracted The coordinator assigns the translation to a qualified translator, ideally a domain SME for the content area. For WHO content, the translator should be familiar with WHO SMART Guidelines terminology. The assignment includes: - The .pot file(s) from extraction - The domain glossary - Context notes (block kind, chapter, content area) - The deadline . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_AssignTranslator . Attach the evidence candidate, extracted The PICO, the graded body of evidence, each verified citation and its resolved authority record are written onto the recommendation block, so a reader can retrace the whole chain from the sentence back to the source. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_AttachEvidence . Attest the pair, with a reason candidate, extracted The prose holds: record it with bun run cat pairs:attest -- --sidecar … --by agent|human --reason "…", naming what was compared. The attestation moves the pair's baseline to the current hashes, so the staleness flag clears and stays cleared until the code moves again. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/narrative-code-review.bpmn#A_Attest . Attribute the failure: each member's own CI first candidate, extracted T2 (SQ19 §2.1 pp. 2-3). A member whose own PR CI is red, or never ran on its head, is the prime suspect, and the evidence is already on GitHub. Only when every member is green alone is the failure a real conflict between them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Attribute . Audit the code nodes the increment adds candidate, extracted Descend into the review task for what this increment CHANGED IN THE GRAPH — Tool definitions in tools/ and schema definition nodes under schemas/. It runs before the summary, and therefore before an MVP can be shared: a Tool or schema node shipped in an MVP is the version stakeholders start building expectations on, and a node that names a skill nobody wrote is cheaper to catch here than after sign-off. Called, not inherited: the agent keeps its implementing role and takes on the code-reviewer lane inside Process_CodeReview for that call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_CodeAudit . Audit the graph candidate, extracted AFTER the change, not before. Every criterion here is a join — role to lane, actor to role, activity to skill — so what an administrative edit breaks is not in the file it edited. The sidecars under test/results/kg-qa/ are committed for the reason a printed verdict is not: without them, "unbound since it was drawn" and "broken by this change" are indistinguishable. Runs kg:audit. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_RunKgAudit . Audit the manifest and schemas candidate, extracted Validate that subgraph-manifest.json conforms to NQuadsDistributionManifestSchema, all referenced partitions exist, and external schema w3c-n-quads is satisfied. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/nquads-distribution.bpmn#A_GateCheck . Author blocks candidate, extracted Every block edit runs the HCI validation gate — see editing-hci-validation.bpmn. A normative statement is a recommendation block, drafted through normative-statements: one statement per block, a folio-chosen label, and its strength as a code in a declared code list, so a reviewer signs off each one individually. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn#Task_AuthorBlocks . Author the fixed test data set candidate, extracted Write the curated records and optional citations with $schema: "test-data-fixed/1.0.0" and kind: "fixed" into the instance's declared test-data-fixed directory (schemas/sdlc/test-data.ts). Recipe fields (template, params, seed) are refused by the strict schema. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-data-curation.bpmn#Task_CurateFixed . Authorise the extraction candidate, extracted The one step no package may relax. A repository cut changes the substrate every other diagram's lanes bind to, and that is a person's decision. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Authorise . Authorise the release candidate, extracted Publication requires authorisation by the programme manager or designated authority. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_AuthorizeRelease . Available to cite as an L1 source candidate, extracted Every knowledge-graph reference to this source now resolves through library/. Authoring and review consume it from here -- see authoring-a-document.bpmn. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Citeable .

2708.title: B
2708.content: Back off candidate, extracted Wait the same intervals backoff-sleep.ts uses, then go round again: fetch the new tip and splice onto it. Three attempts in all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/qa-publish.bpmn#Task_Backoff . Back-translate the target text candidate, extracted Render each target string into the source language, from the target text alone, using no tools, and say so in a TOOLS_USED line that is recorded. A string that cannot be rendered is reported as such, not guessed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-round-trip.bpmn#Task_RT_BackTranslate . Basic ingestion (harness) candidate, extracted The harness's document-ingestion.bpmn: accept the upload by a declared route, extract its metadata into the KG, and catalogue the asset in library/ — placed if materialized, recorded as referenced if not. Everything below refines that result for a document. Called, not copied. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Basic . Bind Requirement front matter, statements, and 3-axis lineage candidate, extracted Author or update the YAML front matter conforming to bootstrap/schemas/requirement.schema.json: id: req:<slug>, title, status, statements[] (each with stable #<key>, RFC 2119 modality MUST/SHOULD/MAY, normative statement, and measurable successCriteria), backward lineage (proposedIn, derivedFrom), horizontal dependencies (dependsOn), and forward links (beans, skills, processes). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/requirements-filing.bpmn#A_BindFrontMatter . Bind the folder to its bibliography slug candidate, extracted Bind the folder name to the document's bibliography slug, so library/<bib-slug>/ and its citation key are the same string: a citation resolves to a directory without a lookup table between them. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_Bind . Bind the test data candidate, extracted Per bean vm6m: a fixed set is a committed path and counts as evidence only once reviewed; a generated set is template + params + seed and is never materialised. Both feed the run's data hash, and nothing that feeds the process hash may feed it too. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-plan-execution.bpmn#A_BindData . Bind Typed Parameters & Execute SPARQL candidate, extracted Safely bind validated parameters into the audited SPARQL template with escaping. Execute SPARQL query against the Oxigraph store. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/named-query-execution.bpmn#A_BindExecute . Bisect the train candidate, extracted Halve the members and re-run the gates on each half until the conflicting one is found: two or three CI runs for three to six members. Only reached when the cheap evidence is silent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Bisect . Blind review per criterion candidate, extracted Criteria: intent-fit, web usability, mobile usability, accessibility, and alternatives considered. A review at one viewport only is incomplete. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#R_Review . Branch, and announce it candidate, extracted Announce the branch WHEN IT IS CREATED, not when the work is done. The gap between one agent's view of an issue and everyone else's is what this closes. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_BranchAndAnnounce . Branch, gates, PR and review candidate, extracted Called rather than restated. The mechanics of getting an edit reviewed and merged are not specific to the role graph, and a second description of them is a second thing free to disagree with the first. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#CallActivity_CodeChangeReview . Branding: does it read as this instance? candidate, extracted Marks, palettes and art against the instance's own declaration rather than a remembered style. The question a downstream folio makes sharp: would this instance inherit something it did not choose? . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Branding . Brief the topic before touching anything candidate, extracted What am I doing and why is it worth doing; what do I already know, with each measurement's provenance; how do I plan to do it and WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THE APPROACH. A falsifier that never fires is decoration. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Brief . Brief the work candidate, extracted What the work is and why, what is already measured with its provenance, how it will be done, and what would falsify the approach. The work item is already taken up when the process starts, so a sibling session sees the work before the brief is written. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_Brief . Brief the work candidate, extracted What the work is and why, what is already measured with its provenance, how it will be done, and what would falsify the approach. The work item is already taken up when the process starts, so a sibling session sees the work before the brief is written. Here the work is a separation: what is separating, and why. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Brief . Brief the work candidate, extracted What the work is and why, what is already measured with its provenance, how it will be done, and what would falsify the approach. The work item is already taken up when the process starts, so a sibling session sees the work before the brief is written. Here the work is a sub-KG: what it is, and why it is staged here rather than in a repository of its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Brief . Broadcast the hold to siblings candidate, extracted Message every sibling that pushes to the repositories involved: what is about to land, and hold pushes, merges and run cancels until done. Ask the coordinator to pass it on to any thread that cannot be reached. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/saturation-meta-merge.bpmn#Task_Hold . Browse in place, emit a KgAsset snippet candidate, extracted Clean degradation when no write capability (git-push, github-api, github-connector) is present: inspect the asset in place through the zero-write browse affordance and output the ready-to-paste KgAsset entry (with source: { instance, path, ref } populated) so the author can apply it where they have write access. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/copy-into-folio.bpmn#Task_InspectReadOnly . Build and QA gates candidate, extracted Lean build and proof status, LaTeX compile, FHIR/SUSHI validation, QA axes. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_BuildGates . Build and review the locale term base candidate, extracted Before translating: build the locale term base from the layered glossaries, review it, and translate with it. Precedence, within one subject area (the scheme's subject): the more authoritative (lower) layer fixes a term's translation; an instance layer only adds. A match in another subject area is a sense check, not a violation. Each layer's glossary is the directory it declares with the glossary graph typology. A fixed translation is an authored term with a non-empty, non-fuzzy msgstr in its scheme's catalogue. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_TermBase . Build each slice into _site at deploy candidate, extracted gen-slice-sqlite.ts --out ./_site/assets/slices --payload-out ./_site/payload/sha256 --slice <name>, once per slice, from the tree being published: the file, its manifest, the slice index, and the deploy payloads beside the committed KG payloads. Never into the committed docs/payload/, whose orphan audit admits KG nodes only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Deploy . Build it locally and measure the file candidate, extracted Run bun run cat slice:sqlite -- --slice <name> --out <scratch> and read the manifest: bytes, the row counts, the payload count and bytes, overBudget, duplicateIds and findings. Record the measurement in the work context with its provenance (the command and the date), beside the size of the source it replaces. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Measure . Build staging site candidate, extracted feature-staging.yml triggers: 1. Regenerate docs (schema, skills, content-backed pages) 2. Render BPMN diagrams 3. Stamp build with commit SHA + timestamp + branch 4. Build Jekyll site with branches/ baseurl 5. Inject yellow staging banner into every HTML page A draft pull request is staged too, from its first push. A build takes about 22 minutes, and GitHub Pages about 3 to 4 more. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-stage.bpmn#Task_BuildStaging . Build the docs site candidate, extracted Build the preview from the PR's head: regenerate the generated docs, trim what this preview does not need, render the BPMN diagrams, then Jekyll, TypeDoc and the knowledge-graph export, with the staging banner and SEO identity claims stripped. It is a PREVIEW build (CAT_BUILD_TYPE=preview, owner 2026-11-01): only what the change reaches, and every whole-corpus index (builtAtPublish entries marked index: true, and the search index) is main's copy, put back rather than rebuilt. A branch frozen for public comment is dispatched with build_type: full instead. Skill feature-staging, section Build types. A PREVIEW REBUILDS ONLY ITS DEPENDENCY CONE (owner cards Q-CONE-1 C and Q-CONE-2 B, 2026-11-01): main's writer records say what each derive:publish writer and each step of the QA working copy READ. A writer or QA step whose recorded reads all match is not run, and main's outputs for it are put back. Every other one runs. QA is not left out of a preview, only narrowed to what the change can reach. Inside a preview's QA build, skill:register also leaves to derive:publish the two pages that derive:publish builds anyway and that no later QA step reads (skills:docs and lsi:viz), so they are built once. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Build . Build the draft publication candidate, extracted Render the corpus into the draft form of the folio: PDF, HTML site, or FHIR IG. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_BuildDraft . Build the entry candidate, extracted First the working copy is produced (qa:refresh, bean 3hk4): while the checkout still tracks test/results/, the commit's own copy is the record and nothing runs; once it does not, every declared QA writer runs into the empty tree, because the gates are in judge mode and wrote nothing a publish could carry. A refresh that leaves a writer failed, a family empty or a file unclaimed is INCOMPLETE: the job goes red and qa:publish --completeness refuses, so a partial tree is never stored as the commit's record — the "Not stored" outcome, reached before any push. Then it hashes the working copy of every declared qa directory (<instance>/test/results/**, byte-identical to the checkout's layout) into a tree through a private index, and writes manifest.json (qa-reports-manifest/v1): inputs, producers, verdict counts and the gates' result. Identical JSON is the same blob, so an unchanged family costs nothing to store again. Its git objects live in a private bare repository, never in the checkout's own store. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/qa-publish.bpmn#Task_BuildEntry . Build the Jekyll site and the API reference candidate, extracted Builds the composed source with Jekyll 4 and just-the-docs (bundle exec jekyll build), runs each composing Tool's post-build pass, mounts instance-rendered content (mount-instance-docs.ts), and generates the TypeScript API reference with TypeDoc (.github/actions/typedoc-api). The main deploy is a full build: every index is rebuilt from the tree being published. See skill feature-staging, section Build types. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Task_Build . Build the L1 knowledge graph candidate, extracted See ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_BuildKg . Build the public comment release candidate, extracted Freeze the draft as "Draft for Public Comment Release vX": a PDF with fixed line numbers and a site copy under a permanent PC/<version>/ path (not branches/, never deleted on merge). Every channel cites this release's pages, lines and block ids. Line numbers run continuously through the document. Freeze from a FULL build: dispatch the preview workflow for the branch with build_type: full first, because a preview borrows main's search index and slices; pc:release freeze refuses a preview build. Run bun run cat pc:pdf for the line-numbered PDF and its line map, then bun run cat pc:release freeze for the write-once copy under PC/<version>/. Skill: document-publishing. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#Task_BuildPcRelease . Build the queue, grouped by owner candidate, extracted Read every bean copy, not only the one this checkout mounts; where copies disagree the newest updated_at wins and the disagreement is listed. Leave out goals and epics, blocked beans, closed or draft ones, owner-held or parked ones, and beans the drainers cannot reach — each with its reason, so nothing vanishes silently. Group the rest by owner in priority order, mark beans other agents hold as skip, and write one shared queue file. The drain-queue Tool (bean n7x7) builds this; until it is defined, the step is the skill's. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-drain.bpmn#Drain_BuildQueue . Build the test run candidate, extracted Assemble the run record the signature will cover: the data hash and the process hash, each all-or-nothing. An UNKNOWN_HASH never reproduces another unknown, so a run that could not be hashed is signable only as what it is — unverifiable. Builds a folio-test-run/v1. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/qa-report-signing.bpmn#Task_BuildRun . bun / pip dependencies candidate, extracted Component 2b. RESTORE: the package managers' download caches, keyed by the lockfile digest (bun.lock; the pip requirements file) and the tool version — never by a hand-listed version string. A restored download is re-verified by the package manager against the lockfile's integrity hashes: class (a). SAVE: main; a PR into its own ref scope. Owner role: the integrator (CI speed 14). cache node: bun-deps, pip-deps. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Deps .

2709.title: C
2709.content: Cancel queued PR runs; build, push, merge candidate, extracted Never cancel a main push run that has started. Build from fresh main with merge commits, skipping conflicts, .github/workflows/ and subscriptions/. Open one PR per repository, merge it with a merge commit, and comment on each member PR with the link. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/saturation-meta-merge.bpmn#Task_Land . Categorize and summarize candidate, extracted Each hit gets a category (overlaps: coordinate; affected by; out of scope; unrelated) and a one-line summary with its state. Judgement, not a keyword score: say why each is in its category. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/related-work.bpmn#A_Categorize . Check before you create (exact-title search) candidate, extracted STRICT. beans create is not idempotent: it mints a fresh id every call and dedupes on nothing, so re-entering a step duplicates the plan instead of no-op'ing. In the qou folio an unguarded re-run produced 14,688 duplicate beans — 92% of every open bean — which starved the idle-backlog policy of signal and collided with 15 real ids. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-open.bpmn#Open_CheckExists . Check disk against lock against declaration candidate, extracted mount:remote:check, with no network: the lock's pins are the declaration's, and every locked directory is on disk and hashes to its digest. Could-not-determine outranks missing, which outranks mounted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_CheckAgainstLock . Check glossary consistency candidate, extracted translation:glossary:check, against the layered term base: the normative reference glossaries first, then each layer in the order the index config lists it, the instance's own glossary last and never overriding. A platform term found in text of another subject area is a sense check for a person, not a violation. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_Glossary . Check glossary terms (translation:glossary:check) candidate, extracted After translating: run translation:glossary:check --instance <dir> --locale <locale>, fix the violations, and include its glossary section in the KG QA report. A term translated against the term base is a terminology miss, so it takes the drift branch to the adjudicator. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_GlossaryCheck . Check Graph Availability Guard (requiredSubgraphs) candidate, extracted Inspect query definition requiredSubgraphs list. Verify that each required subgraph is currently loaded into the Oxigraph store. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/named-query-execution.bpmn#A_CheckSubgraphs . Check it candidate, extracted Look, do not remember. The answer is one of the four states, and "could not determine" is its own answer: a check that could not look is not a pass. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_CheckStep . Check staleness (source hash) candidate, extracted On source content change: computes sha256(source.md) and compares to each translation's status.json sourceHash. If they differ, sets stale: true. The translation remains visible with a "stale — needs re-adjudication" indicator. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_StalenessCheck . Check the .jsonld siblings are in sync candidate, extracted Run the five --check generators in one job — the JSON-LD context, block siblings, library nodes, site graph, then the label-resolution and emitter tests. Any committed .jsonld that differs from what its generator now produces fails the PR, because a stale generated file is still consulted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/jsonld-drift-check.bpmn#Call_Drift . Check the JSON Schemas and JSON-LD are at their IRIs candidate, extracted THE PRIMARY STEP of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness and so the first one checked once the declarations are read. Every JSON Schema the harness publishes (its $id) and every JSON-LD document (its vocabulary, its diagram vocabulary, its graph export, each carrying its own @context) is at the address it names under iriBase, where a program following the IRI finds it. Two checks: that the site build stages each one at its address, and that each address answers. A 404 is not published; a 403 or no answer from here could not be determined. A source that was reachable when the methodology was adopted can stop being so, and a methodology adopted before this axis existed was never checked at all. Measured 2026-09-22: six methodologies cited an origin and NONE had that source in any library, so every selection made until then rested on an unverifiable citation. WHAT A GAP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. A missing source does NOT block the decision, and this step has no branch that stops the process — that would make a documentation gap into an outage, and the owner decides whether an unbacked methodology may still be used. It does two things: it runs literature-search to try to close the gap, and it puts the evidence state into the record A_Record writes, so a reader can tell a decision made on a verified method from one made on a citation nobody could follow. The third state is the one that matters. "Source ingested", "source located but unreachable from here" and "no source found" are three different facts, and literature-search exists largely to stop the middle one being reported as the last. Compose the message candidate, extracted Five required strings — timestamp, actor, process, task, message — and one optional markdown body. The five are required because each answers a question a reader of the log will otherwise have to guess, and a guessed answer in a log is worse than a missing one. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/log-message.bpmn#A_Compose . Confirm all criteria met candidate, extracted The business analyst confirms every acceptance criterion from the requirements is met. The issue closes only on their authorisation — an agent never closes an issue on its own say-so. It IS an adjudication with the requirement-set answers: an approval here moves the set to accepted, which check:requirements refuses unless it is a human's and every approved member is in-force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#BA_Confirm . Confirm main's CI on the merge commit candidate, extracted Read the runs on the merge commit. Red is fixed forward (continual-progress). With no CI the report reads "not verified: no CI", never green. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_ConfirmBase . Confirm needs statement candidate, extracted Stakeholders confirm, on the issue, that the needs statement says what they need — or say what to change. A stakeholder's judgement; an agent does not record it for them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#S_ConfirmNeeds . Confirm the cardinalities candidate, extracted An operational question, asked of the people who run the process because they know where the exceptions are. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#S_ConfirmCardinality . Confirm the entities are the ones meant candidate, extracted A naming question. The BA owns the domain vocabulary; the agent does not guess, which is CRDM's own rule for phase 1 and applies here with more force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#BA_ConfirmEntities . Consolidate findings candidate, extracted One report from however many subprocesses ran. Findings are advice: a reviewer cannot accept the change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_Consolidate . Consolidate into 2-4 themes, with a recommendation each candidate, extracted Group by what the work delivers, not by agent. Each theme gets its epic, members, dependencies, risk, and one of: continue, fold in, new epic, park, scrap (owner only). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#A_Consolidate . Contributor feedback candidate, extracted Process_ContributorFeedback: while the document is a working draft, the Authoring Committee gives feedback through the Contributor Feedback sheet, and each change set is edited and merged in its own pull request. When its changes are merged, the document is validated and rendered again. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/folio-review-publish.bpmn#Call_ContributorFeedback . Coordinate? How? candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/related-work.bpmn#U_Coordinate . Copy asset into target folio and declare in assets[] candidate, extracted Write the asset bytes into a declared path inside the target folio and add the KgAsset entry to the target folio's <name>.json assets[] list (directory-conventions). Never drop the copy into an undeclared scratch directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/copy-into-folio.bpmn#Task_CopyAndDeclareAsset . Create feature branch candidate, extracted Agent creates a feature branch from main. Branch naming: feature/<short-description> Opens a PR immediately (AGENTS.md: "open the PR at the first commit"). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_CreateBranch . Create the bean (agent CLI, not an engine op) candidate, extracted beans create "<title>". This is the AGENT's call. The workflow engine has no create op — its vocabulary is claim, note, resolve and archive, all of which act on an instance's existing bean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-open.bpmn#Open_Create . Create the repositories candidate, extracted The owner creates the content and tools repositories and their Pages. Nothing is committed to them before this. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Create . Create the repository candidate, extracted Only on the new-repo branch, and only after the user has named it. An empty working directory is scaffolded in place instead. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_CreateRepo . Cross the axes into SO, WO, ST, WT candidate, extracted The TOWS matching step, and the only step that produces anything actionable. Strengths and weaknesses across, opportunities and threats down, and each cell names the strategy the pairing implies: SO — achieve opportunities that greatly match the strengths; WO — overcome weaknesses to attain opportunities; ST — use strengths to reduce vulnerability to threats; WT — prevent weaknesses, to avoid becoming more susceptible to threats. A SWOT that stops at four lists is the failure the source names as its central one. This step is what the process exists to reach. It produces CANDIDATE strategies, not a chosen one, and they are not ranked — see the process documentation on why no scoring activity exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_Cross . Cut the subgraph that leaves candidate, extracted Apply the editorial scope mechanically and report what it removed. A selection that reports nothing cannot be told from one that ran over an empty rule. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Select .

2710.title: D
2710.content: Data model Entities + cardinalities candidate, extracted Between requirements and sign-off, and the order is the argument: requirements are statements about things, and the model says what the things ARE. Drafted earlier it is invented from nothing, since the entities come from the phase-2 BPA; drafted later, sign-off approves requirements whose nouns were never pinned — which is how two stakeholders approve one sentence meaning different things. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_DataModel . Decide each adaptation: keep, revise or retire candidate, extracted One recorded decision per affected adaptation, with its reason: keep it as is, revise it to the new version, or retire it because the new version now covers it. A decision to diverge from the new version is recorded as such. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Decide . Decide each theme candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#U_Decide . Decide what may leave the repository candidate, extracted EDITORIAL, and it is stage 1 rather than a filter bolted to the exporter. kg-export produces the WHOLE graph because inspection wants the whole graph; a portal wants what its readers may see. Running the second as the first is how a QA verdict, a bean's blocking note or an unpublished draft reaches a public cache. Decided once, here, rather than at each consumer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#E_Scope . Decide, weighing the recommendations candidate, extracted public-comment decide, or decide: code on GitHub from a login in config.json editors. accepted, accepted-modified, not-accepted, noted, deferred; a reason for all but accepted. Also reopens a decided comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Decide: amend, renew or end candidate, extracted The parties decide what happens to the agreement. Deciding to amend or terminate is human; expiry of a computable agreement is already enforced by its ODRL dateTime constraint. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DecideChange . Declare Distribution Manifest & Named Queries candidate, extracted Write subgraph-manifest.json conforming to folio-nquads-distribution/v1. Declare datasetIri, servedRoute, spine, subgraphs, and audited named SPARQL queries with explicit requiredSubgraphs and typed parameter definitions. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/nquads-distribution.bpmn#A_DeclareManifest . Declare the model where a tool can read it candidate, extracted A model in prose is a proposal; a model in the declaration is a model. Ship a reader in the same change: a model that is only documentation goes inert. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#A_Declare . Declare the mount: harness, repository, pin candidate, extracted An instance { name, source: { remote: { repository, ref } } } in the downstream's root index.config.json, written through writeDeclaredMounts. A folio with no index still reads remoteMounts on its declaration; both at once is refused. ref is a full 40-character commit. Overrides, if any, are keyed by instance name and then by directory id — never by path. The index itself is the index-config skill's. Decide first whether you want a remote mount at all: reading another graph without holding its code is a SUBSCRIPTION, not a mount. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_DeclareMount . Declare the node materialized candidate, extracted The node's state moves from referenced to materialized, carrying purpose, localPath, gates and (archival) fixity. There is NO default state: a node that has not said is invalid, because 'the author did not say' and 'the author said they could not tell' are different facts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Declare . Declare the purpose: working or archival candidate, extracted working or archival, and it is asked FIRST because three of the five gates mean different things under each. An archival copy keeps the original bytes, never expires, requires fixity, and is the only thing that discharges sourceLoss; a working copy keeps derived content and discharges none of that. A process that gated first and asked afterwards would be judging a copy whose obligations it did not yet know. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Purpose . Deduplicate, and keep what is actually relevant candidate, extracted The paper's Refiner. Accumulates into the evidence set the report is built from — so what is dropped here is invisible downstream, which is why it is a step somebody performs rather than a filter buried in retrieval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Refine . Deploy the MVP to staging candidate, extracted An MVP is shared AS A branches/ DEPLOY, not as a description of one. feature-staging.yml publishes the branch under branches/<branch-slug>/ on gh-pages and comments the URL on the PR, so the stakeholder who tests it is looking at the built artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work: holding a rendered change back for assessment makes assessment harder, not safer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_DeployStaging . Deploy the rendering candidate, extracted publish-site.ts commits the staged tree onto gh-pages as a full replace (run by the instance's Pages workflow on a push to main, or by an agent with its own git credentials); GitHub Pages then builds it from the branch. Rebuild and retry on a rejected push; never rebase the branch. The report names the gh-pages commit SHA. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Deploy . Deploy to branches/<slug>/ candidate, extracted The stage job copies the built site into gh-pages under branches/<branch-slug>/, then staging-share.ts apply keeps only the files that differ from the live site. The preview's staging-sw.js serves every other file from the live site and puts the staging banner back on it. Other previews and the main site are left as they are. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-stage.bpmn#Task_DeployStaging . Derive content from the assets candidate, extracted See ingest-derive-content.bpmn. Most of this subprocess is not implemented yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Derive . Derive the key candidate, extracted qa:publish --github reads the event: a push to main publishes under main/<sha>/, a pull request under pr/<n>/<head-sha>/ — the head that was tested, not the merge ref. It also reads whether the token can write, which the gateway after it routes on. The key is main/<sha> or pr/<n>/<sha>. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/qa-publish.bpmn#Task_DeriveKey . Derive the metamodel in use candidate, extracted Tool archimate-metamodel (archimate:metamodel --check, on the instance root): the element types the model uses and every (source type, relationship, target type) pattern, each checked against ArchiMate's relationship table. Placeholder elements named after their own type are reported, never fatal: removing them is the author's call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/archimate-publish.bpmn#A_Metamodel . Derive the slug from the head ref candidate, extracted Derive the slug from the PR's head ref: every character outside [a-zA-Z0-9._-] becomes '-', runs of '-' collapse, and leading or trailing '-' is trimmed. It must be one safe path segment, checked by value. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Slug . Describe the desired change candidate, extracted Author describes the content change in natural language. Example: "Update the immunization schedule to add a booster at 18 months." . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the intended change candidate, extracted The editor states the change in natural language; no content has moved yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the need (chat, issue, discussion) candidate, extracted The BA describes the capability gap in their own words. They do not need to know it is called CRDM. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#BA_Submit . Detect change scope & impact candidate, extracted Agent analyses the requested change: - Which content blocks are affected? - Are there downstream implications (indicators, referral logic, visit schedules)? - Will deterministic logic (CQL/DMN) need updating? skill: content-graph, integration-watcher . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_DetectScope . Detect feature request (crdm-detect skill) candidate, extracted Recognise the request as a platform capability change rather than content work, from crdm-detect's signals. Never call it "CRDM" to the person. Mid-content-work, ask whether to pause for requirements now or record a work item for later — do not switch on your own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#A_Detect . Detect media type, mint a doc id candidate, extracted Sniff the media type rather than trusting the extension, and mint the doc id from the page-1 arXiv stamp where there is one, else from the filename. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Detect . Detect the interaction modality candidate, extracted Before the first question is asked, establish HOW to ask it: audio, ordinary chat, selectable options for a user with limited hand function, large-type for low vision. A user who finds the questions unusable never reaches the rest of this diagram. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_DetectModality . Detect what moved candidate, extracted translation:status --instance <root> for new, obsolete and fuzzy strings, and the instance's template check. Either failing, or showing anything but zero, is a change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Detect . Determine the content type and its specialisation candidate, extracted Read the folio's contentType and the specialisation registered for it (TestDataSpecialisationSchema in schemas/sdlc/test-data.ts): fhir-templating for FHIR IG and DAK content, markdown-fixture for document folios, lean-counterexample for proof folios, tabular-cohort for aggregate indicator tables. None registered stops here and says so, rather than guessing one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-data-curation.bpmn#Task_DetermineSpecialisation . Determine the context: what is known, and already decided candidate, extracted Before composing anything: what is already known, each fact with where it came from; which declaration governs the matter (the instance's <name>.json, the diagram the caller is in, the Skill its task names); what state is recorded; and whether the question has ALREADY been decided — by the person earlier in the conversation, or in a declaration that quotes their ruling. A settled question is not asked again: asking it reopens a decision and spends the person's attention twice. Read it, do not remember it: cite what you read. What the caller handed in is checked here, not re-derived. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineContext . Determine the process and task, or that you are idle candidate, extracted Name the Process, the lane and the task the question belongs to, and say so in the message: "Process: Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent". A reader who does not know which process you are in will assume the last one's rules still hold. If you are in no Process, that is an answer too: you are IDLE, and what you are doing is classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to — say that, rather than presenting a question as though a step had asked for it. You are OUT of process, and it is undetermined, when you cannot name the Process, when two candidates fit, when the step you believed was next is not the one the diagram enables, or when the work in hand was not what you said you would do. Do not infer your way back in. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineProcess . Determine the roles: which you act as, and the person's candidate, extracted An Actor performs a task in a Process AS a Role. Nothing is a Role by nature: the same agent is the Bootstrapping Agent in one diagram and another Role in the next, and which one it is depends on the lane of the task it is performing now. So say which Role you are acting as — the lane of the CALLING task, since this lane is variable — and which Role the person you ask holds (the Requestor, or whoever the calling lane names). It decides what you may ask them for: only the Requestor chooses a harness, and a question put to somebody who does not hold the decision gets an answer that settles nothing. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineRoles . Determine where you are: process, roles, context candidate, extracted Before narrowing, say where this is happening, in the words you will use in the question. PROCESS: Initialize a harness, at its first step, inside Determine the harness and repositories — the only place a Bootstrapping Agent can be (FR-2). If you cannot say that (you were started some other way, or a step you believed done is not), you are out of process: do not infer your way back in. ROLES: you act as the Bootstrapping Agent because you were told so; the person you will ask is the Requestor — the one who asked for the harness, and the only one who may choose it. A request relayed by somebody else leaves the Requestor undetermined. CONTEXT: what the request said, and what the checkout holds — a declaration at its root, a harness named in the request. Whatever cannot be determined is handed to the called discussion as undetermined, and asked about first; it is never filled with a default. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineWhere . Determine which CDN, the root URL and the Subgraphs candidate, extracted Every Subgraph id asked for must be one the declaration lists; none means the whole graph. The root URL is the one given. The target's Tool is the one that satisfies: ["render-kg-to-cdn"] for that CDN — gh-pages for GitHub Pages. A caller that already rendered and verified its tree hands the tree over instead of the graph, and the Tool pushes it without rendering again. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/render-kg-to-cdn.bpmn#Task_Resolve . Determine which harness, and where candidate, extracted The candidates are listed and the Requestor is asked, in discussion, which asks through human-agent-discussion. IN: nothing but the context this agent was handed. OUT: zero or ONE harness, and the locations — a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json. One at most: a list of two is not an answer, and the Bootstrapping Agent may not break the tie itself. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_DetermineHarness . Discard all entries, or a whole session candidate, extracted Remove every entry, one session's, or those before a date — emptyLog with { all }, { session } or { before }; there is no default selector. A file that will not parse is kept, and the result must say what was refused and why, not only what was removed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_EmptyAll . Discard one entry by id candidate, extracted Remove one entry by its stable id, with emptyLog({ id }). Logs are the one exception to the never-delete rule because an entry records no decision; the exception covers files that declare folio-log/v1, not the directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_EmptyOne . Discuss it with the person candidate, extracted Bootstrap's human-agent discussion, given the composed question. Its Ask ONE question step is where this harness's delivery rule applies: Post the whole composed question as ordinary chat text BEFORE any card. This is the copy that survives: a card, once answered, shows only the chosen option, and a dismissed card shows nothing. Never "see the card", never a request for a typed reply such as "1y 2n". Then the card: Whatever the host calls its selection tool (AskUserQuestion, request_decision, a button card): the same letters and labels as the chat text, the recommended option marked. No host card tool: say so in the chat and keep each answer to one short choice. Its answer step: One tap on the card, or any answer the person prefers to give. Free text is always available and never required. A dismissal is NOT an answer and never selects the default as a choice; the question stays open in the chat. On an answer: Hand the answer back to the calling step, quoted. If it settles how a kind of thing is decided, it is a rule: write it into the governing skill in the same turn. On no answer: Do what the question said would happen with no answer, and say so. Nothing irreversible proceeds on a default: such a step waits for the person. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/ask-the-person.bpmn#Call_Discuss . Dispatch one agent, recorded on the bean candidate, extracted Before the agent starts: the date, why the fail condition fired, the agent's id, its budget. Never while the first writer may still be live. Two failed attempts with the same cause go to the owner instead. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Dispatch . Dispatch with adjudicator_sees — never the artefact candidate, extracted UntaintedDispatch on the criterion declares what each party is given; the caller names a subject and a criterion and does not hand-assemble a brief, because the party composing a brief by hand is the producer. untaintedPartitionDefects reports overlap when the checker and the adjudicator can read the same file — one of them is then grading its own input, and the verdict measures nothing while raising no error. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/adjudication.bpmn#A_Dispatch . Distribute to the public candidate, extracted The committee and the editor send the announcement through their channels. Comment is open from here until the agreed close. Skill: public-comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#Task_Distribute . Do it, then check again candidate, extracted Only what the agent, or a tool it has, can do without replacing anything somebody wrote: regenerate a README section, add a missing Pages workflow, switch Pages on with an authenticated gh. Performing is not the same as done: the flow goes back to the check, and only the check says done. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_PerformStep . Do the work candidate, extracted The task itself. This diagram says nothing about how it is done; it only brackets it, so that a reader of the log can tell where one run of work began and ended. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_DoWork . Draft the block edit candidate, extracted The authoring agent produces a PROPOSED change. Nothing is written to the corpus yet. For a rendered change it also produces the before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) here, before Gateway_ValidationFork, so the preview exists when the parallel review starts. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_DraftEdit . Draft, review and publish candidate, extracted See draft-to-publication.bpmn. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#CallActivity_Publication . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_Drain . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Drain . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Drain . Draw the board of todos and beans candidate, extracted The todo board mounts inside the landing board, so harness cards and todo stickies share one surface. Each card carries an edit link only when the build composed one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Board . Draw the sample candidate, extracted On a first translation: every diagram label, every persona and scenario string, and a seeded random fraction of the rest, with the seed written down so the sample can be drawn again. On a refresh: only the strings that were new or fuzzy. Hand the back-translator the msgstr values alone, keyed by an opaque id. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-round-trip.bpmn#Task_RT_Sample . Drop its positions and sweep orphans candidate, extracted Only after the content has moved: drop its positions from the layout layer and sweep any position whose note is now gone. Sweeping first would make the board authoritative over the folio for one step. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_UpdateLayer . Drop the file in the queue candidate, extracted Through the forge's upload form, a commit, or any other route that lands the file in the declared queue. The agent watches rather than chases: an arrival may be minutes or days away. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#P_Upload . Dry-run, then ask the owner naming every PR candidate, extracted Stack the PRs on a meta-merge branch without pushing. Then post the full question (include, leave out with the reason, merge method, per repository), followed by the card: A go, B also the red ones, C dry run only, D cancel. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/saturation-meta-merge.bpmn#Task_Ask .

2712.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, E–Q
2712.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. Its PR says Closes #N for the change-set issue, and opening it moves that issue's accepted comments to editing. Before its preview is staged, the author writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per comment (No. 136: Accepted...), starting from each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, after an optional Overall statement. Agentic status (Green) says where it is, and Staging review opens the preview's what-changed page. 2714.content: Feature sign-off on issue candidate, extracted Stakeholders sign off on the delivered feature on the issue, having tested the built artefact rather than a description of it. Two questions: does it parse as bootstrap's KnowledgeGraphDeclarationSchema, and does it declare at least one harness? could not fetch is a third answer and is never read as conforms. Fixity is REQUIRED for an archival copy: an archive that cannot demonstrate it is unchanged is a copy, and it cannot be re-fetched to check, because the thing it would be re-fetched from is what it exists to survive. The data already exists — every structure.json carries sha256 and bytes, and nothing reads them as fixity. It is drawn as a task because this layer may not name a process of a layer above it; the steps are that process's. RESTORE: read the cached AST from its branch store and judge it — that process's "valid for this commit?" IS this component's verify (class a: the AST is judged against this commit's IG sources and tooling); valid → the site is built from it. SAVE: that process's own path, not cached-step — a miss dispatches an AST refresh on a Java runner with 10 GB, which rewrites the branch store. The branch store is a cache node (ig-ast). Owner: CI speed 12, the IG layers' session. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_IgAst . Filter the corpus, choose the granularity, decompose the question candidate, extracted The paper's Planner. Three outputs, and the middle one is the method's substance: a filtered document subset, the granularity to search at, and the sub-questions. CHOOSING THE GRANULARITY PER QUESTION is the whole point of parsing at several. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. This checkout cannot yet offer the choice — l1-blocks.ts produces blocks, there is no summary level — so this step SAYS which granularity it searched rather than implying the corpus offered alternatives. Re-entered on every iteration, not only the first: the sub-questions are re-derived from what has been found so far, which is what makes the loop a search rather than a retry. Once: an agent that keeps asking has stopped narrowing. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_FollowUp . 2715.title: G
2715.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). A slice whose rows do not match its source fails; it never passes as whole. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Check . Gate results: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 2c. RESTORE: the result store (build/result-store/) and the CI cone records, by prefix — a WARM start: the cone (ci-cone.ts) then matches each stored entry exactly (fingerprint from cache:key --base, every recorded path state, every replayed git answer) and only an exact match is reported SKIPPED, never passed. A committer's local gate record is class (b): honoured on the critical path, then re-verified off it. SAVE: main only (class c for CI's records). Owner roles: the gate-reuse session (CI speed 8) and the committer-side session (CI speed 3). cache nodes: result-store, ci-cone, local-gate-records. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Gates . Gather and verify the evidence candidate, extracted Before anything is drafted: the author reads the guidance ALREADY in this content, frames the question as PICO, retrieves candidates across the three evidence classes, and has each candidate's authority resolved against its publisher's own API. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none -- and the subprocess's first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#CallActivity_Evidence . Generated sets: QA copy, pages candidate, extracted Component 2d. RESTORE: the QA working copy and the publish-time pages, keyed by bundle-cache.sh digest (the tree and the exact tool versions). A bundle is checked against the manifest it carries AND a source rule (the source run's head is this head, a parent, or a commit with this tree; or a main-scoped save) — class (a′), because a manifest alone proves a bundle intact, not built from these inputs. Hits across commits wait on the producers being byte-reproducible (the determinism audit). SAVE: the run that built it, recorded; main's records are read by every branch. Owner role: the generated-sets session (CI speed 10); the preview's copy, the preview session (CI speed 2). cache nodes: qa-working-copy, publish-pages. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. 2719.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. Until 2026-10-09 this was two steps here, Task_Release in the owner's lane bound to interaction-modality and Task_Land bound to prepare-merge; neither could refuse a merge, and neither said what happens when a repository has no CI. R1 still holds: what lands is exactly what CI tested. If main moved after the train's CI started, re-run rather than land.
