Drawn as its own end state because a destructive action whose refusal is not drawn gets performed by accident. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_Cancel . Link L1 nodes into the corpus graph candidate, extracted Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact -- paper, L2, L3 -- resolves to it through library/. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_Link . Link the work to an issue candidate, extracted Feature work must be linked to a GitHub issue. Scan before creating, and never create one without the BA's permission — an issue is the stakeholder's record, not the agent's scratchpad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Issue . Link to existing issue candidate, extracted A match was found: ask the person whether the requirements go on #NNN, then link the work there. The issue is where stakeholders sign off, so no phase proceeds without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_LinkIssue . List the harnesses this could be candidate, extracted Zero or more. The candidate everybody has is bootstrap itself. Context may name others: "please set up <owner>/<repo> here" names one, and so does any Harness built on bootstrap that the Requestor mentions. This step narrows; it does not decide. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListHarnesses . List the locations this could install to candidate, extracted Zero or more. Is this a git repository already, or were one or more URLs to repositories supplied? Both are Knowledge Graph Data Stores; the difference is only how they are reached. A location whose root already holds a declaration, <name>.json, is not a blank slate, and says so in the question. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListLocations . List the steps the declarations name candidate, extracted In the order of the table in initialization-steps: declaration, needs, each dependency's instructions, the documents at their IRIs (checked above; the report leads with them), directories, assets, README, README sections, site. Each step names the declaration that names it, so a reader can see why it is there. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_ListSteps . List upstream releases and compare to the pin candidate, extracted git ls-remote --tags, filtered by the row's tagPattern and ordered by version. Nothing is cloned and no API token is needed, so the check runs the same way on a laptop and in CI. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_QueryUpstream . Load the active voices candidate, extracted The activated set only, never everything shipped. An id naming no shipped voice is an error rather than a skip — a folio that believes it is applying a voice and is applying nothing has the cleanest-looking output of the three. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_LoadActive . Log a message or an error candidate, extracted Write a message or error entry whenever a later reader would need it. A command run goes in execution (command, exit code, where output went) — never the output itself, and never a secret, token or credential: capture on puts entries in git. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogMessage . Log findings on the bean candidate, extracted Findings are appended to the bean, so the next agent or human sees what is outstanding. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_LogFindings . Log task-end candidate, extracted Write a task-end entry, with the outcome in the detail. The step is the unit: an entry per step, not one when the whole process finishes, or every intermediate entry is lost. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogEnd . Log task-start candidate, extracted Write a task-start entry before touching anything: summary, actor, and the process/task/bean/branch/session it belongs to where they exist. role, process and task are optional on purpose — do not invent a lane for work done outside a process. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogStart . Log the failure candidate, extracted Every failure path passes through here, so "logged as failed" is a step somebody performs rather than an adjective on an end event. What differs between the ways in is the message, which is an input, not the mechanism. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_LogFailure . Log the start of the install candidate, extracted REQUIRED logging, which is what drawing the call says. Logged before anything is written, so an install interrupted halfway is distinguishable from one never begun. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_LogInstallStart .

2721.title: M
2721.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. An agent may be dispatched to run it on its own: it needs nothing but that diagram and the declarations. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_CompleteInitialization . Make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it candidate, extracted Provisioning the target, owned by this process rather than by the publication step that calls it. Pages cannot serve a branch that does not exist, so in order: (1) an orphan gh-pages branch exists — git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, push a placeholder (index.html + .nojekyll); (2) Pages is on, Source = the gh-pages branch at / — gh api -X POST repos/<o>/<r>/pages -f source[branch]=gh-pages -f source[path]=/ when gh is signed in, otherwise the exact manual step (Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages, / (root)). Each half is done, not done, or could not be determined; never assumed. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Provision . Make the change candidate, extracted The loop's only open-ended step. Everything around it is procedure; this is the work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Implement . Make the change candidate, extracted content-change-review-make.bpmn: scope the change, branch, edit content and logic, assess and absorb the downstream impact, and push. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_MakeChange . Make the change, check it and merge it candidate, extracted The second phase, drawn on its own page (public-comment-change.bpmn): an author edits the document as decided on a feature branch, the change set is reviewed on its staging preview, an independent QA gate checks the dispositions against the pull request, and each comment it answers is marked incorporated when it merges. A withdrawal still interrupts the comment while this runs. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#CallActivity_MakeChange . Map the affected layers in order candidate, extracted Run the re-pin planner (mount:repin:cone) with the fleet and the changed repository. It lists every site downstream in waves, so a site moves only after the layers it takes from have moved, and marks which sites are ready now. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_MapCone . Map values onto palette roles candidate, extracted surface / ink / edge / accent, shared across every kind. A palette per kind would be three spellings of "accent colour", free to disagree about what an accent IS. Where the source is SILENT on a role, say so and mark the value a choice rather than dressing an invention as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/ingest-theme.bpmn#Task_MapRoles . Mark every copy answered candidate, extracted Chat copies keep their text: the question struck through and "[Edit: <letter> chosen by <who>, <time>]" added. Cards closed with the chosen option. The sheet's "Decision needed" block replaced by the decision and who made it. Withdrawn or superseded hand-backs marked the same way, with the reason. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_MarkAnswered . Mark incorporated when the change set merges candidate, extracted public-comment incorporate, naming the branch, PR and staging URL; done by the folio's workflow when the PR that closes a change-set issue merges. A PR closed unmerged moves nothing. Ready for merge is set only once the QA gate has passed for the PR's head commit; set earlier, the agent does not merge until it passes. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary that closes its issue. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_Incorporate . Mark it skip on the queue candidate, extracted Record on the queue file that the bean is held elsewhere, and by whom, so no other drainer takes it next. The bean itself is not touched: closing or noting on someone else's bean is how a sibling loses work it had not finished reporting. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-drain.bpmn#Drain_Skip . Mark the record superseded or retired candidate, extracted Never delete (git rm) a superseded or retired requirement. When superseding req:<old-slug>, set status: superseded and supersededBy: req:<new-slug> on docs/requirements/<old-slug>.md. When retiring, set status: retired and document the retirement reason and authorising issue in prose. Update any RequirementSet (docs/requirements/*.set.json) so approved/accepted sets hold only in-force members. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/requirements-filing.bpmn#A_UpdateLifecycle . Materialise the part candidate, extracted The ONLY way bytes arrive. Purpose first, then the five gates — size, restrictions, copyright, retention, source loss — then fetch with fixity, or stay referenced with the refusing gate's basis recorded. Both ends of that subprocess return here and the walk continues: one part refused is not the subscription refused. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Materialize remote content (the five gates) candidate, extracted The shared subprocess. It resolves the request against the source descriptor, then asks size, restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, and either fetches with fixity or leaves the content referenced. This process does not restate any of that; it waits for the outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Measure the cutover: separation:cutover:check candidate, extracted Run bun run cat separation:cutover:check --site in the SEPARATED repository (Tool separation-cutover-check). Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate and none assumed: every declared layer mounted at its pin; every path a declaration names resolves (check:declaration-resolution — directories, assets, visualisers, needs); no wiring still names the monorepo (livesAt, a submodule, a reusable workflow, a path into the old checkout); no import or reference against the layer order; and the site builds from the mounts alone. A finding inside a mounted layer is upstream's and is listed, not counted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_CutoverCheck . Measure the signals candidate, extracted Files and bytes per instance, clone cost (bun run cat health), gate time, merge contention, the candidate's cohesion and cut (kg:detangle), wrong-direction edges, and the would-be tools package's import cone. Recorded in the work context; none alone is a trigger. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Measure . Mechanical checks, both viewports candidate, extracted Tool wireframe-check renders every candidate at a web and a mobile viewport. It fails on horizontal overflow at mobile width, on placeholder text, and on a missing viewport, and writes screenshots and a script entry per criterion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Check . Merge and publish candidate, extracted content-change-review-publish.bpmn: merge on the owner's explicit confirmation, then remove the staging preview, rebuild main and watch it. An unmerged change keeps its preview. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_Publish . Merge each member onto the base candidate, extracted merge-base.bpmn once per member, in order, --no-regen; then ONE bun run cat regen over the result. Tool: merge:train. Always onto the current base, never a cached one (R5). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Call_MergeMembers . Merge into each locale candidate, extracted Merge each refreshed template into every locale's catalogue: new strings arrive empty, changed ones fuzzy, and obsolete ones are kept as #~ entries, never deleted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_MergeLocales . Merge main in, regenerate, fix mechanical gates candidate, extracted Merge commits only; never a force-push. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_AgentFix . Merge the base in, without committing candidate, extracted git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main on a clean tree (untracked files refuse too, so the final stage cannot sweep in a scratch file). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the one source PR to main candidate, extracted All the templates in one PR to main, merged before any locale starts, so every translator branches from the same main. Once it has merged, its branch receives nothing more: a later fix to the source is a new PR. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_SourcePR . Merge the PR candidate, extracted Merge the instance's PR to main, then confirm the template checks pass on main. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Merge . Merge the pull request candidate, extracted The agent merges the row's pull request, and Agentic status says merged. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary: it goes into the merge, and closes the change set's issue. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the re-pin with its decided revisions candidate, extracted The re-pin merges when its checks are green and every decision it needs is recorded. Its pull request cites the decisions, which become the release notes for this site's update. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge train candidate, extracted Ready PRs that stack land as a train through merge:guard. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn#Call_Train . Merge, hold or refuse candidate, extracted The owner's answer to the question Task_Ask asked. Their words are quoted verbatim in the record, so the answer is given in the conversation or on the PR, not inferred from tone. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_OwnerDecides . Merge, on explicit confirmation candidate, extracted The owner says "merge it", and only then is the branch merged. Merge to main triggers: 1. the main site rebuilds with the changes; 2. the staging preview's cleanup runs; 3. the review comments committed on the feature branch land on main, as the review record. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-publish.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge, pinned to the evaluated head candidate, extracted Through merge:guard <pr> --merge --session <id> where the repository has it; elsewhere with the merge call pinned to the head SHA, so GitHub refuses if the head moved. Merge commit unless the repository or owner says otherwise. Never delete the branch. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_Merge . Mirror it to the feedback channel candidate, extracted Review sheet: the "Decision needed" block in the row's agent column, Agentic status Needs you (the document layer's review-sheet-script skill). Issue or PR: a comment. An extra copy, never instead of the discussion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Mirror . Mount each instance at its declared path candidate, extracted Sparse checkout of the declaration and the chosen directories, copied to the mount path (by default the instance's home path, so relative imports and sibling discovery hold). Never onto tracked bytes; never onto a directory no lock says this mount made; never over edits to a previous mount — those are left untouched and reported. A replay of the lock tries the index's layers cache ref first (refs/cat/layers/<key>, then refs/cat/layers/main): one shallow fetch, every byte verified against the lock, and any layer that does not verify is fetched from its own repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_MountInstances . Mount the branch tip at the declared path candidate, extracted A branch source keyed by tip: branch-store mount --id <dir-id> writes the tip's files at the declared path, so every reader finds the directory where it always was; push splices edits back onto the tip, never forcing, and a same-file race is a conflict. The branch's NAME is the declaring directory's storage (or source) — a branch no declaration names is refused rather than guessed. A commit-keyed branch is read per commit through its own store (qa-store), not mounted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountBranchTip . Mount the remote tree at its pin candidate, extracted A remote source: another repository's tree at a full 40-character commit. bun run cat mount:remote lays it down at the declared path and locks its tree digest; it is never written back, because the bytes are somebody else's at somebody else's pin. Usually reached through a source.remote instance in the root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts), which expands a whole harness and its closure — Process_MountDependency. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountRemotePin . Move into library/<bib-slug>/ candidate, extracted The folder name IS the bibliography citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Promote . Move the entry's ref and re-cache the declaration candidate, extracted Only after every held part has been through the refresh. Moving the ref first would make the records of parts not yet refreshed describe a commit the entry no longer names. The cached declaration is replaced so the review that follows shows what the NEW pin offers, including subgraphs that did not exist at the old one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_RePin . Move the pin and open the PR candidate, extracted The pin literal moves in the one file upstream-pins.json declares, and the PR body says what the version range changed in RENDERED output — the evidence, not just the verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_ApplyPin . MVP: build the candidate on a staging branch candidate, extracted An MVP is a DEPLOYED BUILD, not a description of one. The pin is moved on a branch and feature-staging.yml publishes it under branches/<branch-slug>/, so the reviewer looks at the artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Task_Mvp .

2722.title: N
2722.content: Name the subject and the level candidate, extracted One sentence naming WHAT is being analysed and at WHICH level — individual, organisational, national, international. The source requires this before anything is listed: "the classification of a variable also depends on the purpose of the practice", and the criteria for assigning a variable to a quadrant "may be more difficult to clarify if the methodology is not used for a company but for a country". It also bounds the known limitation that SWOT "is rarely deployed at lower than the organization level", where one scan drives strategy for units its factors do not hold equally for. Naming the level does not remove that risk; it makes it visible in the record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_FrameSubject . Name the substrate, pin a full commit SHA candidate, extracted owner/repo and a 40-character commit SHA — never a branch, never an abbreviated SHA. The schema refuses anything else (SubscriptionSchema.ref), and this step exists so the refusal is met while choosing rather than at commit time. A tag replaces the SHA only once the substrate publishes releases. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Pin . Name what will move, and where it lands candidate, extracted Before anything moves, name the content that would move — what it is, with its size and age — and where it lands. The confirmation sits in front of the move: an agent never relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_AskConfirm . Narrative description per image, localized candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF, not only to an uploaded one. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Image . Narrative review candidate, extracted Descend into Process_NarrativeReview. The actor takes on the narrative-reviewer lane for this call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_NarrativeReview . No CI: run the repo's own gates locally candidate, extracted Only on no-ci. Run the repository's own gates (its tests, typecheck and whatever its README or package.json names) on the merge result, not the branch. Record each command, exit code and the SHA it ran on. This is evidence the owner can weigh. It is not CI, and the question to the owner says so in words. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_LocalGates . Note the bean, summarise on the issue candidate, extracted The merge SHA and the authorisation block on the bean; a round summary on the issue (issue-working). The issue is not closed here: in CRDM, crdm-close closes it after this process returns, on the BA's authorisation. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_Report . Note the main-branch watch candidate, extracted Second dispatch point: the change was approved and merged, and the root of the site has been rebuilt from main. A failing main build can look like a green run from inside the repo. note rather than claim: the branch-watch bean already exists, and whether the publish SUCCEEDED is not this step's judgement (the build reports its own exit code). A bean is not closed on someone else's say-so, so the step records what it observed and leaves the verdict to the watcher. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-publish.bpmn#Task_WatchMainCI .

2723.title: O
2723.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval"), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-extract-structure.bpmn#Task_Ocr . Offer KG destinations for the agreed set candidate, extracted Without this step, agreed and signed-off requirements exist only as an issue and a conversation, and the knowledge graph never learns them. ONE question for the SET, not one per requirement: a six-phase run can agree many, and asking six times is the same failure as a form that re-asks what it was already told. The options are DERIVED from the graphs this instance declares in <name>.json, read at the time of asking, so an instance that adds a graph gets it in the offer without anybody editing a skill. Never a list typed from memory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_OfferKg . Open a bean for the unverified citation candidate, extracted An unresolvable citation is not dropped and not silently kept. It becomes a tracked item, so the gap is visible in the work plan rather than surviving as a footnote nobody re-checks. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_RecordUnverified . Open beans for the change requests candidate, extracted Each requested change becomes a bean, so the editors and agents picking the work up next see exactly what review asked for and what is still open. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_OpenChangeBeans . Open or close a role to an actor candidate, extracted The join every other diagram depends on. An empty roles is a DETERMINED empty — it says the actor takes on none — and is not the same as an absent one, which asserts nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AssignRoles . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted Findings: EDIT the one open issue carrying the tracking label (the label input) if there is one, otherwise create it, with the report as the body. One issue edited in place, never a new issue or a comment per run, so the tracking issue never becomes a feed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_TrackIssue . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted One issue, edited in place. GitHub's own failure mail is the channel that was already ignored thirty times, so this adds none: an edit does not notify, and a pin that stays behind for two months stays one unread item rather than nine. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_TrackIssue . Open or edit the one tracking issue candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/tracked-watch.bpmn#Task_Track . Open the bean candidate, extracted Process_BeanOpen on the bean just taken: check it, find out whose it is, and claim it — or leave it alone when another agent holds it. OPEN's check is where the drain's claim check runs (the bean-claim-check Tool, bean n7x7): recent commits on every bean copy and any open PR naming the bean, before the claim. The gateway after this reads which end OPEN reached. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-drain.bpmn#Drain_Open . Open the bean candidate, extracted Check before you create (exact-title search), create the bean when none exists, find out whose it is, and claim it — or leave it alone when a sibling holds it. Process_BeanOpen is the one place a claim is drawn. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-lifecycle.bpmn#Call_BeanOpen . Open the bean candidate, extracted Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else's. The one place a claim is drawn (bean m8gz, owner 2026-10-24); the gateway after this reads which end it reached. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_ClaimBean . Open the bean candidate, extracted Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else's. The one place a claim is drawn (bean m8gz, owner 2026-10-24); the gateway after this reads which end it reached. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Call_BeanOpen . Starting the watcher and recording that it is running are ONE declared step, so the two cannot disagree about whether anything is watching. It notes the watch on the bean rather than claiming it: only Process_BeanOpen claims a bean. The note is idempotent, so re-entering on a later push does not duplicate it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/publish-alert.bpmn#A_Open . Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. Not between Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_RecordDecision: Flow_21b runs Task_RecordDecision -> Gateway_EditorDecision, so the gateway reads a decision already recorded. In the Agent lane: the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED (its own decision-audit note), and Task_RecordDecision in Lane_Editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN. The analyst is not the decider. (CallActivity_Evidence is in Lane_Editor because the author performs the retrieval.) On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief's trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached Task_ReviewFindings with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis adopt · hold · decline candidate, extracted On the single edge into PM_Decide, and deliberately not earlier: the MVP build and its gates are HOW the options' costs are measured, so an analysis before Task_Mvp would weigh alternatives against no evidence. Everything the decider needs exists by the time the reviewer has finished and the fixable findings are fixed. In the Agent lane, because this step produces the analysis and does not make the decision — PM_Decide is a userTask whose lane admits person only, and putting the analysis in the agent's lane is what keeps that separation legible rather than implied. A subprocess that decided would be a second accepting party. Reached through the loop as well as straight through: SF_UA_8 re-enters at A_Impact, so a run where the reviewer found something fixable arrives here a second time with different evidence. That is a genuine re-analysis and its op="note" appends rather than deduping, which is the behaviour wanted — a second note records that the options were weighed again against changed inputs. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. Not between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact: those are in different processes with no sequence flow between them; the assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the committee review is where a decision is taken. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator (from Task_EditLogic) does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. By Phase 6 the needs, requirements and data model are signed off, which is exactly the evidence an options analysis needs and the reason it belongs here rather than earlier: at Call_Needs there is nothing to weigh, and after A_Implement the choice has been made in code. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries a note on the bean (its claim is the OPEN that Process_CRDM calls first); this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Organise entry in docs/requirements/index.md by concern group & status candidate, extracted Add or update the requirement's row in docs/requirements/index.md under its canonical concern group (sdlc, process, tools, kg, library, content, ui, conduct from code-lists/concern-group.json) for in-force requirements, or move it to the Superseded and Retired Requirements table when superseded or retired. 2724.title: P
2724.content: P1.1 · Agree the terms candidate, extracted The parties agree the purpose, the datasets, the period, the conditions and duties, which trust anchors each side accepts, and the legal basis the sharing rests on (consent, treatment, public-health law or a research waiver). This sets what the text must say; it is a negotiation between people. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_AgreeTerms . P1.2 · Write the legal text candidate, extracted Write the agreement as a document folio: one normative statement per clause the parties must keep, through normative-statements. The text says which governs if it and a machine-readable form disagree (suggested: the text). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_WriteText . P1.2a · Record the legal basis candidate, extracted The text states the legal basis the parties agreed in P1.1 as a normative statement: consent, treatment, public-health law, or a research waiver. Consent rule 1: only an agreement whose legal basis is consent carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty; treatment, public-health law and research waivers do not rest on consent. The gateway that follows, the ODRL and the reviewers all read the basis from this statement. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_RecordLegalBasis . P1.2b · Draft the plain summary candidate, extracted Consent-based only. Write a plain-language summary of the agreement in the same document folio: what it lets the recipient do with the person's data, in words the person can read. Consent rule 3: every agreement that needs consent publishes this summary, hashed with the agreement (P2.2a), and the summary is what the person consents to. It is reviewed, rendered and versioned with the text. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_PlainSummary . P1.3 · Derive the ODRL 2.2 Agreement candidate, extracted Computable only. One assigner and one assignee (ODRL 2.2 §2.1.3), permissions and prohibitions with target assets (§2.2), constraints (§2.5.1) and duties (§2.6.3), written as JSON-LD. Purposes from HL7 PurposeOfUse. Consent rule 1: the Agreement carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty only when the legal basis recorded in P1.2a is consent. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DeriveOdrl . P1.4 · Check the ODRL against the text candidate, extracted Computable only. A person checks that the ODRL says what the text says, and signs it off. A program can check the ODRL is well formed; it cannot check that it matches the text. The check includes the consent duty: present when the legal basis is consent, absent otherwise (consent rule 1). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_CheckOdrl . P1.5 · Split public terms from private annexes candidate, extracted Split the agreement into a public template and private annexes (security controls, named staff). Only the hash of a private annex is ever published. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_SplitAnnexes . P1.6 · Sign candidate, extracted The signatories sign: wet ink, or an electronic signature under national law. Technically a detached JWS (RFC 7515) or CMS (RFC 5652); PAdES for a signed PDF needs the owner's approval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Sign . P14.2 · Decide what happens to existing grants candidate, extracted Existing grants keep citing the old hash. The parties decide, per agreement: they stay valid until expiry, or they are revoked and reissued against the new version (in smart-trust). The old version stays readable. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DecideGrants . P14.3 · New consent needed candidate, extracted The amendment widens use, so a Consent citing the old version's URL and hash does not cover the new version (consent rule 2). Record on the bean, and in the new version's text, that new consent is needed; the new version gets its own plain-language summary (P1.2b). Asking each person again is the trust layer's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_NewConsentNeeded . P14.5 · Set the status to ended candidate, extracted Set the life-cycle status of the agreement's DCAT 3 record (DCAT 3 §6.4.30). The published versions stay readable at their URLs. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_SetStatus . P2.1 · Assign version and fixed URL candidate, extracted Each signed version gets its own immutable URL (for example /dsa/42/v3). A 'latest' URL may exist; nothing cites it. A new version never overwrites an old one. This fixed-version URL is the one a Consent cites (consent rule 2), and a computable agreement's ODRL policy uid is set to it (P2.3). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_AssignVersion . P2.2 · Record each file's SHA-256 candidate, extracted Compute SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) of the signed text, and of the ODRL file if there is one, recorded as DCAT 3 spdx:checksum and verified by check:dsa-hash. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Hash . P2.2a · Hash the plain summary candidate, extracted Consent-based only. Record the SHA-256 of the plain-language summary beside the agreement's, in the same version (consent rule 3). The summary a person consented to can then be checked against the agreement it summarises; a changed summary is a new version. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_HashSummary . P2.2b · State the URL and hash to cite candidate, extracted Consent-based only. The version's publication metadata states the fixed-version URL (P2.1) and the hash (P2.2) that a Consent cites in FHIR R4 Consent.policy.uri (consent rule 2), never the 'latest' URL. For a computable agreement that URL is also the ODRL policy uid (P2.3): a Consent counts only when its Consent.policy.uri equals the agreement's ODRL policy uid, so the two are the same string. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_ConsentCitation . P2.3 · Make the ODRL cite the text candidate, extracted The ODRL policy names the signed text distribution with dcterms:source (DCMI Terms), pointing at the immutable URL whose spdx:checksum was just recorded. Its uid is that same fixed-version URL, the URL a Consent cites in Consent.policy.uri (consent rule 2). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_OdrlCitesText . P2.4–5 · Write the DCAT 3 record candidate, extracted One DCAT 3 record: the agreement as a catalogued resource, each file a dcat:Distribution with dcat:downloadURL and spdx:checksum; datasets it covers carry odrl:hasPolicy. Versions are linked with DCAT 3 versioning (previous version, version, current version). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Catalogue . Package with digests candidate, extracted The serialization alone is not a package. A package is an addressable set — the JSON-LD, the assets it references, and a manifest naming every file with its digest and byte count. The manifest is what makes a REMOVED file detectable, which a per-file signature cannot do on its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Package . Persist the log to the data store candidate, extracted Capture is explicitly on — by <cat-harness.processes:log capture="on"/> on the process or by config — so the entries go to the git data store. Only this branch commits anything. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_PersistLog . Phase 1 Needs candidate, extracted Identify the stakeholders, synthesise a needs statement from the sources, and loop until the BA and the stakeholders both recognise it. The loop is the phase: a needs statement nobody confirmed is an agent's summary, not a requirement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Needs . Phase 1: Identify stakeholders candidate, extracted The agent asks the BA who is affected by this change. The BA knows the domain — the agent does not guess. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#A_Stakeholders . Phase 1: Synthesise needs from sources candidate, extracted From the chat, issue, uploads and library sources, write a clear, jargon-free statement of what is needed and why, tied to a concrete workflow. Post it on the GitHub issue, not in chat, and ask the requester and stakeholders to review it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#A_Synthesise . Phase 2: Map current workflow (BPA) candidate, extracted Business-process analysis here means reading the existing diagrams under processes/ and drawing the gap, so the skill that implements this step is the BPMN one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_MapWorkflow . Phase 4a: Compare the viable options candidate, extracted Phase 4 often ends with a CHOICE rather than a plan, and this is the step that hands it over. Per option: what it does, its pro, its con, what it changes DOWNSTREAM, and how reversible it is — laid out where the rows can be read against each other, then one recommendation and a stated default. A step of its own rather than a line inside A_DefineReqs, because it has a different output and a different reader: the impact analysis is for the record, the comparison is the thing the BA answers from. Folding it in is how it gets skipped — the analysis feels finished, so the options go over as a list of names. When Call_Wireframe ran, its wireframe candidates are among the options: one row per candidate, with a link to its web and mobile screenshots. Skipped legitimately when the analysis yields ONE viable approach. Do not manufacture alternatives to fill a table. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_CompareOptions . Phase 5 Plan + sign-off candidate, extracted The approved requirements become work-plan items, the BA signs off, and the branch is announced on the issue. The announcement is on the single edge into delivery, so the three loops back into implementation do not re-announce. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Signoff . Phase 5: Create beans candidate, extracted The agent mints the implementation beans itself with beans create, running the exact-title existence check first. The engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean — so what this step records here is a note that the plan now exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_CreateBeans . Phase 6 Implement + acceptance candidate, extracted One phase and not three, because the loops say so: an increment the BA rejects, an MVP that is not ready, and stakeholder findings all route back into implementation. A subprocess has one exit and cannot be re-entered once finished, so splitting this region would have changed what the diagram says. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Deliver . Phase 6: Implement (feature branch + PR) candidate, extracted Inner loop: agent claims a bean, implements on feature branch, opens PR, posts summary to the issue. When the requirement changes a rendered surface, implement against the wireframe candidate the requester or BA chose in Phases 3–4 (Process_WireframeDesignReview, called from Process_CRDM_Requirements), not against a fresh design; and the delivery summary links the chosen candidate beside the after-screenshot, so the reviewer can see the build matches what was approved. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_Implement . Phases 2–4 BPA + requirements candidate, extracted Map the current workflow, then define the requirements and the impact they carry, and loop until approved. Same shape as Phase 1 and for the same reason: an unapproved requirement is a proposal. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Requirements . Phases 3–4: Define requirements + impact candidate, extracted Two skills, because this step is two things: the requirements come from the CRDM process, the impact half is a question about the entities and relations the change touches, which is what data modelling answers; a folio-content skill such as content-graph is not one this harness diagram can bind. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_DefineReqs . Pick up the stale pin candidate, extracted The hand-off from the mechanical lane to the one that can exercise judgement. Claiming the bean here is what stops two sessions adopting the same bump. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#A_PickUp . Place by ownership; declare the directory candidate, extracted A domain-neutral method belongs to the harness and a domain method to the folio that owns the domain. If the session cannot write where it belongs, draft it where it can, say so in the file, and open a bean to move it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/methodology-from-source.bpmn#A_Place . Place it by hand, with a reason candidate, extracted Recorded as a queue entry whose placement is override with a position and a reason; the schema refuses one without a reason. It enters the next placement as the table's ownerOverride input. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Override . Place it in uploads/ by a declared route candidate, extracted THE FIRST LINK: everything downstream of here takes a file that is already in the queue, so without this step how the file got there is governed by nothing. WHAT THIS STEP IS. The basic flow's ACCEPT step: choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the instance that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one can 404. WHY A PLAIN bpmn:task AND NOT A userTask. A userTask asserts a human performs it, and this lane is "Contributor (human or agent)" because both do; asserting human-only would be an activity-fulfilment-kind contradiction. A plain task asserts nothing about the performer. WHY THE BEAN OP IS note AND NOT claim. Placing a file claims nothing; it adds to a queue. What it owes the work plan is visibility. A note against the ingestion bean is what makes the queue's growth something another session can see. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Place . Place the asset in library/<slug>/ candidate, extracted The materialized branch. The asset lands in library/<slug>/ with its metadata record, its provenance and its fixity. The folder name IS the citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string. The upload is then RETIRED, not left and not deleted: it moves to fsh-guts/uploads/ beside a sidecar naming where it came from and when, and check:uploads-retired finds one that was not. A refining process that derives content from the bytes does so before that retirement; library-ingestion carries the rule. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_PlaceInLibrary . Plan scope, team, artifacts candidate, extracted Scope the work, identify artifacts and actors, form the team, set the timeline. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Plan . Plan the document candidate, extracted Scope it: chapters, the blocks each needs, which statements are normative. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn#Task_Plan . Plan the prune candidate, extracted Keep every main/<sha> for 90 days and one per day after that; drop pr/<n> 7 days after the PR closed. 2725.content: QA gate: check dispositions against the people and the pull request candidate, extracted Before Ready for merge. Writes: QA gate (change set), first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. Now the qa-working-copy job builds it once and uploads everything the build changed as an artifact with a sha256 manifest; each reader downloads it, checks the manifest against the hash this job reported and every restored file against the manifest, and only then judges. 2727.title: Glossary: BPMN activities

2729.content: Every term the instances in this repository define or carry, as W3C SKOS. Terms link to the external concepts they match rather than copying them. 4099 terms: 41 authored in 6 glossaries, one page per instance that owns them, and 3976 extracted from knowledge-graph assets in 15 generated schemes, one page per asset type, plus the sources below. | state | what it means | terms | . | authored | A person wrote or approved the definition. | 41 | . | candidate, extracted | Lifted from a knowledge-graph asset's own title and description, verbatim, and not curated. 2730.title: Already somebody else’s concept?
2730.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 4019 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 4019 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin.

2731.content: Each term is on exactly one page. Authored terms are on the page of the instance that owns their scheme (owner, 2026-10-15), and extracted candidates are split by asset type (owner, 2026-09-24), so that no page is fetched at the size of all of them. | page | holds | terms | size | . | this page | counts and sources | — | 11 KB | . | bootstrap | authored terms of bootstrap | 22 | 28 KB | . | cat-harness | authored terms of cat-harness | 14 | 19 KB | . | folio-assistant-core | authored terms of folio-assistant-core | 4 | 10 KB | . | who-iris | authored terms of who-iris | 83 | 224 KB | . | Skills | candidates, extracted | 322 | 248 KB | . | Tools | candidates, extracted | 26 | 31 KB | . | BPMN activities | candidates, extracted | 905 | 760 KB | . | DMN decisions | candidates, extracted | 15 | 12 KB | . | Schema fields | candidates, extracted | 2708 | 1.6 MB | . Size: this page is 11 KB before compression, within its budget of 64 KB; each instance’s and each asset type’s page has a budget of 1.0 MB. 2935.title: Already somebody else’s concept? (غير مترجَم)
2935.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. (غير مترجَم) . The table’s labels are in the source language: it reports counts per scheme, computed by the gate rather than authored here. (غير مترجَم) . Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 4019 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 4019 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin.

2940.title: computable adjudication and agentic test harness
2940.content: Computable adjudication and agentic test harness. Also written: caaat-harness, ca&at-harness, .c&at-harness, c@t-harness . Please be introduced to a cat who acquires things, for whatever purpose — maybe somebody knows. Scope: the platform — skills, schemas, processes, the MCP server and the pipeline. Not what a folio IS (that is folio-assist-core), and not any folio’s own content, which lives in its own repository. | cat-harness, in the source Its own repository since the cutover; the in-tree copy is archived in folio-assistant’s fsh-guts. | RTFM — the cat-harness docs The agent–user interaction model, and what this harness is for. | The work plan is where you say what you are doing Claim a bean before you work, so a sibling session does not pick up the same item. | Make your first folio This repository is the platform; your content lives in its own. | Know which kind of thing you are writing A document is structured prose; a paper adds the block kinds whose assertion is a formal claim. | The documentation you will never read All of it. The honest expectation is that you arrive from a search engine when something breaks. | .

2941.title: What a folio is
2941.content: The knowledge graph is four sub-graphs, and an instance declares which of them it holds. Content is what somebody authors and a reader reads — this layer’s subject. Skills are the instructions an agent follows to do the work. Processes are the BPMN diagrams that say who does what, in which order, and where the gates are — they are executable, not illustrations. Tools are what an agent can call. Getting anything in is acquisition: unstructured and semi-structured sources arrive through uploads/ or through the conversation, and are ingested into library/. It is a step rather than a graph typology of its own — there is no fifth directory to look for. Scope: the content model — what a folio IS. Not the skills and tools that operate on it, and not any particular folio’s chapters. | Content A document is structured prose; a paper adds the block kinds whose assertion is a formal claim. | Skills Every skill and role, and how they fit together. | Processes The BPMN diagrams, which are the source of truth rather than a picture of it. | Tools What an agent can call, served over MCP. | Acquisition How a source gets from uploads/ into library/. | RTFM — folio-assist-core Its scope, in and out, and why it declares no directories yet. | .

2945.title: What this site is
2945.content: . | The IRIS-style home — IRIS’s home page, rendered from this repository’s catalogue and themed as IRIS, at this site’s root. Each held item links to its library entry page; communities and collections go to the catalogue page. It is an ingested copy: not WHO, and not live. | The catalogue — what the catalogue knows, and what it records that it does not know. Every node declares whether its bytes are here (materialized), elsewhere (referenced) or unestablished (unknown), and there is no default. | The gap is the point. IRIS reports its own figures for items and files; the catalogue holds a few and models the rest by reference. The census is bun run check:catalogue, never a number written into a page. | . This repository is the development home of the instance; an official copy is expected to live under WHO’s own account.

2949.title: Lanes — who acts
2949.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Writes four records in a fixed order and touches the corpus graph in none of them — dublin-core as the record of truth, a manifest that references it, assets[] kept as a SIBLING of library: because that tree is regenerated and would drop anything written inside it, and finally the slug binding Task_Link depends on. 2950.doc: Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph
2950.title: Steps
2950.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Write dublin-core.jsonld (the record of truth)Task_Dublin | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | One standalone Dublin Core record per folder. dcterms is already this corpus’s JSON-LD vocabulary, so this extends a live context rather than introducing one. | . | Write manifest.jsonld referencing itTask_Manifest | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write manifest.jsonld for the folder: its @id, @type folio:SourceDocument, what it contains and its provenance, referencing the standalone dublin-core.jsonld as the record of truth rather than copying its fields. | . | Record assets[] — local path or remote URLTask_Assets | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | kind / role / url-or-path / checksum / retrieved. A SIBLING of library:, never inside it: LibraryRef is regenerated from the tree, so an authored URL placed there is dropped on the next sync. | . | Bind the folder to its bibliography slugTask_Bind | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Bind the folder name to the document’s bibliography slug, so library/<bib-slug>/ and its citation key are the same string: a citation resolves to a directory without a lookup table between them. | . | Read glossary and abbreviations into candidate termsTask_Glossary | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | glossary-terms | The source’s glossary and abbreviations sections become candidate terms of a folio-glossary/v1 scheme with the Tool glossary-from-source, verbatim, each with source file#line, and an acronym as the notation of the term it expands. Terms a person owns are never changed, and only a person moves a term to authored. A source with no such section skips this step with nothing written. | . | Link L1 nodes into the corpus graphTask_Link | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact – paper, L2, L3 – resolves to it through library/. | .

2959.title: Lanes — who acts
2959.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Two provenance paths converge on the same Task_Sections output — an embedded text layer extracted directly, or OCR that leaves the fuller text in ocr/ with only a stub in sections/ — and which branch this lane took is invisible downstream except to a grep that knows to check the fourth tier. Task_Candidates stays a proposal: nothing downstream may treat it as an adjudicated verdict. | .

2960.title: Steps
2960.content: Every one of the 5 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Extract the text layerTask_ExtractText | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The document has a text layer: extract it with pdf-extract (pdfminer.six, then a zero-dependency content-stream reader). Exit 2 means no text layer — a scan — and routes to OCR; it is not an empty document. | . | OCR to ocr/page-*.txtTask_Ocr | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently (“Manual” and “Manval”), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. | . | Split into sections/*.md with doc_brief front-matterTask_Sections | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Contextual retrieval: a chunk in isolation loses what makes it mean anything, so each section carries the document brief. | . | Write structure.jsonTask_Structure | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write structure.json (pdf-structure/v1): doc id, TOC from the PDF outline or inferred from headings, page ranges, metadata, and source{} with the sha256 and a mimetype sniffed from the bytes, never the extension. A structure that could not be determined says so in structure_note rather than being rendered as one. For OCR’d text, source.runContext cites the OCR step’s run context by sha256. A title already known for the document (the catalogue’s dc.title, or one given with –title) is passed through as the raw title, so the sections’ doc_title does not carry a scan’s misreading. | . | Extract claim candidatesTask_Candidates | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | candidates.json holds extracted theorems and definitions. Proposals only – never adjudicated verdicts. | .

2975.title: Every initialization step, as the declarations name them
2975.content: Skill initialization-steps: Walk every initialization step the declarations name (the instance’s own and each one it needs), check each before doing anything, do what can be done, ask for what only a person can do, and report every step as done, not done, could not determine, or stated. Named by: Complete initialization, Determine the harness and repositories, Initialize a harness . You are making sure a harness’s initialization is complete: right after installing it (initialize-harness calls complete-initialization), or because you were dispatched to do exactly this with nothing but the diagram and the repository. Either way the steps are the same, and they are not listed in this file. They are named by the declarations.

2976.title: Where the steps come from
2976.content: Read <name>.json at the root, then each name in its needs, from a sibling checkout at ../<name>/<name>.json. Each step below names the declaration that names it, so a reader can see why it is there. | step | named by | done when | . | declaration | the file itself | <name>.json parses and its name is its file name | . | needs:<name> | needs | the dependency is beside it, and its declaration parses | . | instructions:<name> | FR-4 | stated: <name>/docs/bootstrap/initialization.md was read and followed | . | schemas:staged | each $id / @id under iriBase (FR-11) | the site build stages every JSON Schema and JSON-LD document at its IRI | . | schemas:published | the same IRIs (FR-11) | every one of those IRIs answers | . | directory:<id> | directories[] | the declared path exists | . | asset:<id> | assets[] | the declared file exists | . | readme | FR-8 | the root has a README.md | . | readme-sections | the README’s own markers | every section the README opts into is current | . | site:workflow | repository | a workflow commits the rendered site onto gh-pages | . | site:branch | repository | a gh-pages branch exists — it must, before Pages can be switched on | . | site:enabled | repository | Pages is on, serving gh-pages | . | site:live | iriBase, else the Pages address | the address answers | . The two schemas: steps are the primary ones. They are checked first once the declarations are read, and the report leads with them: publish-documents. A harness above bootstrap names more steps the same way. A work-plan store it declares as a directory is a directory: step, and a harness’s own set-up instructions are its instructions: step. Bootstrap does not need to know which harness declares what. The site steps are in publish-site.

2977.title: Four states, not two
2977.content: . | done: checked, and it holds. | not done: checked, and it does not. Say exactly what to do next. | could not determine: the check could not run (no forge CLI, no network). Never reported as done. A check that could not look is not a pass. | stated: the declarations name it but nothing can observe it (reading and following a harness’s instructions). Follow it, say you did, and leave it stated. | .

2978.title: Idempotent by construction
2978.content: Check before doing, every time. A done step is left alone, so running the process twice changes nothing the second time, and an interrupted run is resumed by running it again. Performing is not the same as done: after you do a step, check it again, and only the check says done. Replace nothing. A step that would overwrite what somebody wrote (an existing README, a Pages site built from a branch, a declaration that disagrees with the directories on disk) is a step for the person. Ask through human-agent-discussion, with the exact step written out. Do not create an empty declared directory to make its step pass. Git does not track an empty directory, so the check would pass on your machine and fail on every clone. Put its first file in it, or ask whether the entry should go.

2979.title: Where tools are available
2979.content: A toolset may perform the checks for you — for example https://github.com/litlfred/bootstrap-tools, whose init command reads the same declarations, does what a tool can (regenerating README sections; switching Pages on when an authenticated gh is present), and prints each step in these four states with what to do next: . bun run scripts/init.ts --root ../<instance> # from a toolset checkout beside it bun run scripts/init.ts --root ../<instance> --dry-run # check only . Where no tools are available, do the same by reading files. The diagram is the same either way, and so is the report.

2980.title: The report
2980.content: One report through log-message, led by the primary step’s state (the JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at their IRIs): then every step, the declaration that named it, its state, what was seen, and for anything not done, what to do and who does it. End with the counts (done, not done, could not determine, stated). An initialization that finished with steps open says which. It is not hidden behind “installed”.
